## Summary

Describe the change and the problem it solves.

## POWER methodology check

- [ ] Authority claims identify the actual institution or office with power to act.
- [ ] Evidence is distinguished from interpretation.
- [ ] Unknown or unresolved claims remain explicitly unknown.
- [ ] Appropriations are not presented as expenditures.
- [ ] Implementation is not presented as outcome.
- [ ] Outcomes are not presented as proof of causation.
- [ ] Partisan conclusions, endorsements, or simplistic political rankings are not introduced.

## Civic-data / evidence check

- [ ] New factual civic claims have exact source URLs, dates, and jurisdictions.
- [ ] The source supports the claim actually being made.
- [ ] `establishes` / `doesNotEstablish` boundaries are preserved where applicable.
- [ ] Demo records are clearly marked as demonstration data.
- [ ] No placeholder source is labeled as verified.

## Accessibility / UX check

- [ ] Keyboard and focus behavior remain usable.
- [ ] Plain-language explanations are preserved or improved.
- [ ] Mobile behavior has been considered.
- [ ] Status is not communicated by color alone.

## Validation

- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [ ] `npm run audit:public-release`
- [ ] `npm run build`

## Notes / limitations

List unresolved questions, known limitations, or follow-up work.
